harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1’s RHEL-native Apache 2.4.63 service on TCP/8080. The staged help tree is served under /help/, /manual URLs return permanent HTTP 301 redirects preserving path and query strings, and /status.txt returns the supplied document directly. SELinux remains enforcing, firewalld permits 8080/tcp, source checksums are unchanged, and all behavior persisted through a verified node reboot. RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 were retained.
actions_performed: Captured platform, listener, service, security-control, file-permission, and source-checksum baselines.
Installed Apache from the configured RHEL repositories.
Configured Apache to listen on port 8080 and serve /srv/legacy2/permanent-url-migration.
Added exact permanent redirects from /manual and /manual/... to the corresponding /help/ URLs.
Applied persistent SELinux content and port policy and opened only 8080/tcp in firewalld.
Enabled httpd and verified direct content, redirect, query-string, status-document, and negative-route behavior.
Rebooted node1 safely, confirmed its boot ID changed, and repeated service, content, security, and integrity checks.
Confirmed no failed units or temporary verification residue remained.

evidence.requirement: Serve the staged help tree on TCP port 8080
evidence.summary: Apache listens on 8080 only; /help/ and /help/network/setup.html return HTTP 200 with bodies matching the staged files before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Permanently redirect old manual URLs while retaining path and query string
evidence.summary: Both base and nested legacy URLs return HTTP 301. The nested test preserved /network/setup.html and the full mode=compact&lang=en query, followed exactly one redirect, and returned the expected staged body.
/status.txt returns HTTP 200, has no Location header or redirects, and its response checksum matches the supplied status document.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the operating-system release, kernel, source data, access, and security controls
evidence.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 remain installed; all three source checksums are unchanged. SSH and firewalld remain active, SELinux remains enforcing, Apache workers use the apache identity, and there are no failed units or temporary-test remnants.
Apache configuration reports Syntax OK; the port-8080 virtual host, persistent SELinux mappings, permanent firewall rule, enabled service, and requested HTTP behavior all survived reboot.

Healthy baseline boot ID 2db46909-a020-4fda-b1db-2c3ead04c18a was captured; the safe systemd reboot was acknowledged; recovered boot ID 14c6aa3d-e4b8-454f-85b4-50a67fa50a14 proves a node restart; system state, SSH, firewalld, SELinux, Apache, listeners, source checksums, redirects, help content, and status content all recovered.
